material_definitions: The investigation focused on electrical properties and crystal structure for ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
Conductivity was enhanced both by Li2O addition to the LiHf2(PO4)3 system and by increasing x in Li1+xMxHf2-x(PO4)3 (M = Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu or Y).
The P21/n monoclinic phase transitioned to the NASICON-type R3c rhombohedral phase above 1173 K.
This phase transition decreased the activation energy for Li+ ion migration, with the bulk activation energy for the NASICON structure measured at 0.42 eV.
The materials are solid solutions of LiHf2(PO4)3 + yLi2O (where y=0.1 in this case).
Li2O acts as a flux to achieve high-density pellets and contributes to conductivity enhancement.
The high conductivity is primarily attributed to the formation of the NASICON-type rhombohedral phase (R3c) upon sintering above 1293 K.
The maximum conductivity (1.1 x 10^-4 S cm^-1) was obtained for the sample sintered at ca. 1298 K.

material_definitions: The Li1+xMxHf2-x(PO4)3 (M=Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y) systems are ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
Samples were sintered above 1293 K to achieve a NASICON-type structure (R3c) and high density.
The maximum conductivity of 1.7x10^-4 S.cm^-1 for the entire system was achieved by this specific sample (x=0.2, M=Fe).
The Hf-system is considered superior for applications like batteries because Hf4+ is more stable toward lithium metal than Ti4+.
